items.title: Toone, Beever-Jones return for Lionesses ahead of WC play-off
items.excerpt: Sarina Wiegman has named 25 players for England’s decisive FIFA Women’s World Cup play-off against Ukraine, with Ella Toone and Aggie Beever-Jones returning to the squad.
body: Sarina Wiegman has named 25 players for England’s decisive FIFA Women’s World Cup play-off against Ukraine, with Ella Toone and Aggie Beever-Jones returning to the squad.

Toone was initially excluded from the camp to face Greece in October with Wiegman saying that she had not "played to her potential". She earned a recall following an injury to Lucy Bronze, having impressed with her reaction to the setback.
Chloe Kelly was also a notable absence from the last squad, but this time misses out due to a hamstring problem that has kept her out since the end of September.

Beever-Jones returns having last featured for the Lionesses in their 6-1 victory over Ukraine back in March. She takes the place of Chelsea team-mate Lauren James who is sidelined. items.title: 'Outstanding' Dowman scores historic winner as England U21s beat France
items.excerpt: Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest ever goalscorer by grabbing a late winner in a 3-2 victory over France at Ashton Gate.
body: Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest ever goalscorer by grabbing a late winner in a 3-2 victory over France at Ashton Gate.

The 16-year-old Arsenal prodigy became England's youngest Under-21s player last week in the defeat to Portugal - but made even more history by popping up with an 89th-minute winner on his second appearance, as he played the entire game. How the teams lined up | Match stats

At 16 years and 320 days old, Dowman is the youngest-ever goalscorer for England at this level. The previous record was held by current England men's senior star Jude Bellingham - who broke the record aged 17 years and 67 days against Kosovo in September 2020.

body: Martin Tyler is more convinced than ever he will finally get the chance to commentate on England winning a major international trophy after watching Thomas Tuchel's side's 3-2 Uefa Nations League victory in Spain

The legendary football commentator, whose new book 'Tales from the Gantry: Letters from a Lifetime in Football' was published on Monday, knows a thing or two about England teams, good and bad, having called over 350 Three Lions internationals while attending an astonishing 13 World Cup finals during a decorated 53-year career that is still going today.
The book is "historical", says Tyler. "It is what I was thinking about in football that week. There's 110 different essays, half a dozen of them were letters from America.

"I wrote 500 words a week for two and a half years. It starts early in 2004 and finishes in July 2026." England's win over Spain in Madrid means they have finished top of the group.

That matters as the winners of the Nations League tier A groups are seeded for the quarter-final draw. They will play teams which have finished runners-up in other groups. They will also play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.
